risks
risks · 4 records
  1. Customer default or dispute can require enforcement; letters of credit pay only on specified default/breach.
  2. Price bands have floors and ceilings; SCA floor-margin claim is management expectation and depends on cost/yield/mix.
  3. Deposits return if minimum purchase commitments met; unrestricted cash does not mean permanently surplus.
  4. Forced purchases can leave customer inventories and ultimately worsen market oversupply.

ROICReview
ROICReview · 4 fields
reported Comparable ROIC
Not specified / unresolved (null)
status
not reliably derived as a clean through-cycle return from current endpoint balance sheets
reason
Peak pricing, construction in progress, incentive-reduced PP&E, refundable customer financing and very large excess marketables distort endpoint invested capital. ROE or EBIT/book equity is not ROIC. Forecast terminal ROIC is an explicit judgment (base12%, bull18%, bear9%).

cash Flow Conversion Note
FY2026 CFO 89,675 less gross capex 30,712 = 58,963. Company adjusted FCF 62,308 equals CFO less net capex 27,367; gross capex is reduced by cash government incentives 3,316 and PP&E-sale proceeds 29. Deposits of 12,747 are financing inflows, not operating FCF.

capabilities
capabilities · 5 records
  1. domain
    demand forecasting
    assessment
    Strong near-term visibility in the observed boom; through-cycle forecasting remains uncertain.
    confidence
    medium
    evidence
    evidence · 2 records
    1. 8 consecutive revenue outcomes at or above original midpoint; six above original range.
    2. SCAs make portions of minimum demand/pricing enforceable.
    outcome
    FY2026Q2 and Q3 revenue exceeded original midpoints by roughly 27.6% and 23.7%, indicating material underforecasting during scarcity.
    counterexamples
    counterexamples · 3 records
    1. FY2023 operating loss and earlier inventory correction show cyclicality persists.
    2. FY2025Q2 gross margin was below midpoint; recent sample omits a completed downturn.
    3. Customer purchases to fulfill commitments can build inventories and amplify the next bust.

thesis
Near-term contracted scarcity supports FY2027 growth, then industry cleanrooms and equipment arrive and pricing resets in FY2029-FY2030. HBM differentiation lifts normalized EBIT above FY2025, but does not perpetuate 80% margins.

5
maturity Years

maturity Rationale
Five years capture the new-fab/contract horizon and a pricing normalization; another five allow through-cycle economics to settle. A 15/20-year high-growth extension would be hard to defend in commodity memory.

thesis
AI/customer capex stalls, supplier capacity arrives, market pricing drops despite partial SCAs, inventories rise, and a loss year precedes recovery. FY2027 revenue falls short of sequential-growth management expectation.
early Explicit Years
5
maturity Years
10
maturity Rationale
Five years capture the new-fab/contract horizon and a pricing normalization; another five allow through-cycle economics to settle. A 15/20-year high-growth extension would be hard to defend in commodity memory.

maturity Revenue Unit
USD millions
investment Policy
Use direct gross capex, government cash, D&A and operating NWC in the first five years. Negative growth never mechanically liquidates fabs. After year 5 use marginal sales/capital, fading to terminal ROIC-consistent economics. Do not subtract both direct cash investment and sales/capital reinvestment. Incentives reduce asset basis and D&A; projected D&A uses net-basis judgment. Do not add gross-basis D&A to grant-net capital expense without reconciling depreciation benefit.
tax Policy
Normalized cash operating tax; loss-year tax benefit is not monetized immediately. Deferred tax and geographic incentives can change cash timing.
sbc Policy
Recurring SBC remains an operating expense. No FCFF add-back without an offset for dilution or repurchase cost; award-overhang bridge remains open.

invalidators · 5 records
  1. CY2027 bit-supply agreements or SCA price floors are materially renegotiated; customer defaults or inventory accumulation become visible.

  4. Construction cost/late yields cause gross capex or replacement needs to exceed schedule; grants arrive late.
  5. Positive-growth terminal returns cannot be sustained without materially more reinvestment.

valuation Timing Policy

2026-10-17
operating Model Convention
end-of-year discounting from latest reported annual/TTM baseline; illustrative operating EV only
unresolved
Precise stub-period cash generation, distributions, new financings and post-balance-sheet claims must be rolled to valuation date before per-share release.
forecast Status
Independent analytical scenarios; all current and unresolved claims retained; no implementable equity recommendation or per-share output.
capitalization Policy
capitalization Policy · 4 fields
reported EBITBasis
Reported GAAP operating income for MU; TIFRS operating income for TSM. No synthetic starting-margin rewrite.
research And Development
Keep reported R&D expensed. No research-asset capitalization or amortization adjustment has been made. If a later model capitalizes R&D, it must restate both operating profit and invested capital consistently across history and forecast.
software And Leases
Maintain reported treatment in starting facts; detailed software/intangible additions and lease roll-forwards remain in final cash-flow reconciliation. Do not capitalize operating expenses merely to lift margins.
SBC
Recurring SBC remains an expense; no add-back that ignores dilution.
maintenance And Capital Path
maintenance And Capital Path · 7 fields
maintenance Definition
Economic replacement and technology-refresh spend is not separately reported. D&A is an audit proxy, not evidence that economic maintenance equals accounting depreciation.
early Years
MU direct gross capex/grants/D&A/NWC in years1–5; TSM net reinvestment with implied capex/D&A audit. Fixed commitments and technology refresh remain during downside.
later DARevenue Ratio
0.18
later Grants
MU cash-grant forecast ends after year5; TSM ordinary support embedded in net capital-efficiency judgment, with no extra asset.

bounded Model Gaps
bounded Model Gaps · 6 records
  1. Valuation-date stub and post-anchor cash/claims/share roll-forward not integrated; this is a forecast-origin operating EV, not October 17 equity value.
  2. No probability weighting or share-price calibration. Source forecast assumptions are judgments, not reported facts.
  3. Enterprise-to-equity bridge is not computed here; consult the company-specific claim register for resolved evidence, assumptions and remaining uncertainties. Zero is not evidence of absence.
  4. Negative-growth years still incur direct fab investment. No nonnegative revenue-growth/S:C adapter can represent these rows.
  5. Customer deposit repayments, grants and dilution require separate consistent claim/forecast treatment.
  6. Final explicit revenue growth is 2.5% versus terminal growth 2.0%; preserve the published path and disclose this endpoint change alongside the capital convention transition.

required Changes
required Changes · 4 records
  1. Versioned direct annual schedule input and durable import/save/restore; do not substitute a flexible-profile-generated path.
  2. Operating-only calculation independent of cash, debt and shares, with equity/claims gates retained.
  3. Expose final-explicit 2.5% growth versus terminal 2.0%; any smoothing or endpoint revision is a new sensitivity, not a silent adapter correction.
  4. Direct net-reinvestment override; do not clip negative growth to zero investment.
